commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Undermine is a top-down dungeon-crawling roguelike where you play a humble miner collecting gold and upgrades. It looks basic and has nothing structurally unique, and the early game deliberately feels underpowered. Once you get past the start, items synergize so well that you become absurdly overpowered and can break the game. He finds it packed with content and modes, and has returned to it many times. He calls it a really good game and places it in A tier.
praise: Huge number of items that synergize insanely well
Extremely easy and satisfying to break the game and feel overpowered
Packed with content: blessings, pets, customization, multiple game modes
Classic Roguelike mode is amazing and worth playing by itself
Looks basic but executes its fundamentals very well
Strong replayability; he has come back many times
criticism: Feels underpowered at the start, which is not a good feeling in roguelikes
Must grind the early game before unlocking the best content like the Classic Rogue mode
Game can crash or have duplication glitches when broken
unique_points: Deliberately starts you weak (lore of a random miner saving the world) then flips into power fantasy
Overpowered broken builds are intended, even showcased in the trailer via infinite duplication
Post-completion game mode gives a reason to keep playing after you have become overpowered
commentary.quote: this is a really really solid game uh this is an easy a tier for me
comparisons: Dungeon of the Dungeon (likely the 'dungaree' he mentions, ASR-mangled, discussed earlier in the video)
design_criteria: Item synergies: many items combine into game-breaking builds
Power curve: weak start then overpowered payoff
Content and mode variety: pets, blessings, customization, alternate modes
Meta-progression: grinding early game unlocks late content
Replayability: extra game mode gives reason to return after mastery
Combat depth: basic fighting is a minor weakness

community.one_liner: A top-down, pixel-art action-adventure roguelite by two-person studio Thorium in which a peasant delves an ever-changing mine, blending Zelda-style combat and exploration with RPG-like gold, relic and permanent-upgrade progression.
community.consensus_summary: UnderMine is well received: Steam shows about 90% positive across roughly 9,900 reviews (Very Positive), and critics on Metacritic rate the PC version 79 and the Switch version 83, praising its polish, presentation and upgrade systems while noting it does little unexpected. Player opinion splits on its heavy meta-progression: fans call it a satisfying one-more-run loop with lots of secrets, while detractors find the early game weak, grindy and RNG/curse-driven. It left early access (Aug 2019) for a full 1.0 launch on Aug 6, 2020 with Xbox Game Pass inclusion, then came to Switch (Feb 2021) and PS4 (Mar 2021). The studio has since moved to UnderMine 2, which some recent reviewers read as a sign the original is mostly finished; the Steam store page shows a soft recent-review dip (small sample).
best_things: Polished, charming pixel-art presentation and fitting music, often highlighted even by players who dislike the gameplay loop
Strong sense of progression: failed runs still unlock upgrades, items, NPCs and permanent improvements, fueling a 'just one more run' feel
Huge amount of secrets, events, hidden rooms, recipes and achievements to discover, including after beating the main story
Rescuable helpers/NPCs with their own skills and permanent perks add RPG-style depth
Combat and relic/potion synergies can produce fun, sometimes absurd builds late in a run
Flexible pacing: you are not forced to rush or beat every boss each run, and post-game challenges and difficulty adjustments add replay value
Plays well on both gamepad and mouse-and-keyboard; easy to pick back up casually
Critics call it well-constructed, with clear mastery of controls, upgrade systems and overall design (Nintendo Life 90, Hey Poor Player 90)
worst_things: Grind is the top complaint: incremental meta upgrades make early runs feel intentionally weak and unfair
Many items and relics are seen as minor stat boosts that do not change how you play, so builds feel samey
Item pool and content variety are limited: the same items keep reappearing and only a few bosses repeat every run
Annoying or artificial difficulty: traps at room entrances, bomb-filled trapped chests, sliding off ledges, enemies swarming with little room to dodge
Curses and scarce healing can ruin an otherwise good run, which reviewers describe as anti-fun
Gold does not carry over between deaths, making it hard to save up for big purchases
Melee versus the ranged/boomerang option is seen as unbalanced, with the first boss hard to hit in melee
Some players report slightly delayed controls after actions, unclear item descriptions, and room mechanics with no explanation
improvements: More varied weapons or starting loadouts, since the base attack set never really changes
More impactful, build-defining relics rather than small numeric boosts
Greater variety in bosses and items, and post-game challenges that add new content instead of only self-imposed handicaps
Smoother early-game balance: faster gold, less RNG around healing and curses, less reliance on meta grind
Clearer in-game explanations of item effects and room interactions
Clearer in-game explanations of item effects and room interactions (already listed) and more polish on control responsiveness
Tighter control responsiveness; some reviewers note delayed actions when timing matters
unique_things: Gold-and-greed loop: you mine gold, spend it on upgrades and lose part of it on death, with a peasant-fodder dark-humor story
RPG-flavored stats, potions and shopping layered over Zelda/Isaac-style action, which some reviewers say suits RPG fans more than hardcore roguelike fans
Persistent NPC/helper rescue system and a huge web of hidden recipes and secret rooms
'Othermine' mode, praised as a purer start-from-zero roguelike experience once found
Mine that changes every run, with the freedom to descend at your own pace rather than speedrun
tedious_or_disliked: Grinding meta currency to get modest damage or stat boosts, which some call padding that stretches limited content
Repetitive loop of samey rooms and enemies after the first dozen hours
Having to survive many runs just to reach later bosses, especially for new players who die early
Low-impact relic drops and RNG-locked synergies that make good runs rare
Keys, bombs and healing feeling too scarce to open most of a floor
divisive_points: Meta-progression: some see satisfying RPG power growth, others see a grind that replaces good balance
Difficulty and RNG: curses, traps and heal scarcity read as fair challenge to some and as cheap to others

Originality: critics call it polished but unsurprising, and users compare it to Binding of Isaac, Enter the Gungeon, Moonlighter, Hammerwatch and early Zelda, sometimes favorably and sometimes as less complex or charming
Roguelite versus roguelike expectations: RPG fans like the progression, traditional roguelike fans are more likely to bounce
community.reception_notes: Early access began Aug 20, 2019; 1.0 released Aug 6, 2020 on Windows and Xbox One (Game Pass), Switch Feb 11, 2021, PS4 Mar 30, 2021; Wikipedia says about 600,000 downloads across Steam and Game Pass by Jan 2021, and SteamSpy-style estimates put Steam owners at 500k-1M. Third-party estimate (steam-revenue-calculator.com, Boxleiter method, treat as order-of-magnitude) is about $6.1M gross and $1.8M net on Steam. Critics were warm at launch; user reviews are split more sharply than critics, and Metacritic user score (7.0, 29 ratings) is mixed and listed on the Switch page. UnderMine 2 was announced Apr 2024 and is out, leading some reviewers to say the original is effectively finished. A live web search was not possible because the search budget was exhausted; Reddit and OpenCritic pages could not be fetched, so OpenCritic score is null. Steam store page also showed a recent-review dip (Mixed, small sample) that I could not verify further.
